name: Pin Release Reversal
note: A dated, mechanically-caused distortion faded the session after it expires. On an expiration Friday the close is compared with the nearest listed strike K on a hardcoded grid ($1 below $25, $2.50 to $200, $5 above); the name must have PINNED (within pin_frac of the half-interval, which is the largest distance to a strike that can exist) and must have been DRAGGED there (its close lb sessions earlier at least drag*G away from K). The trade is entered market-on-open the next session in the direction the stock came FROM -- long if it was above K, short if below -- and closed at the close of the hold-th session after. Two honest notes. The band is a fraction of the half-interval rather than of G itself, because 0.05*G is a 10%-of-the-possible-range window that fires about once per symbol per quarter; the literal version is pin_frac=0.1 and it is in the sweep. And expiry defaults to WEEKLY Fridays (monthly_only is swept) because a 120-day study window contains five monthly cycles, which cannot reach the per-symbol trade minimum -- the monthly-only variant is included so the sweep can say what it is worth, not because it can clear the bar.
source: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (2005), JFE 78(1), 49-87 -- Figure 1 panels (clustering by trade date -10..+10) and the reversion-to-non-manipulated-level argument in Section 5.
